text: In McTaggart's terminology, the A-series orders events by which properties, and the B-series by which relation?
choices: The A-series orders events by past/present/future; the B-series orders them by the earlier-than/later-than relation.
The A-series orders events by earlier-than/later-than; the B-series orders them by past/present/future.
The A-series orders events by simultaneity; the B-series orders them by causal priority.
The A-series orders events by their spatial location; the B-series by their temporal location.
explanation: For McTaggart the A-series runs past-present-future (positions that change, and that A-theorists take to be fundamental), while the B-series is the permanent ordering by earlier-than and later-than. Option 1 simply swaps the two series; the point to fix is that the A-series carries the tensed, changing A-properties.
